subject: [Action] Stratton-lite v2: staged version hold + interop questions
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Patrick O'Neill <patrick@stratton.ai>, Stratton Labs Model Ops <deploy@stratton.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Alan Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [Action] Stratton-lite v2: staged version hold + interop questions

Hi Patrick / Stratton team,

Thanks for sharing the v2 artifacts this morning. Product flagged a couple of potential regressions in our initial evals and I want to propose a short, staged approach before full entry. Specifically:

- We saw a tokenizer divergence on long-form prompts (prefix tokens differ in ~0.6% of samples) which can affect caching and replay determinism.
- The model's KV cache layout appears to increase per-request memory by ~12% at 2k context; this will impact throughput for multi-tenant Dedicated pools.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Place a 7-day staged version hold in model-catalog for stratton-lite-v2 (prevent rollout to Hosted production routes).
2) Run a compatibility smoke plan in Staging (small corpus + perf telemetry + tokenizer diff report). I attached a short smoke plan (compat-smoke-plan.md) and would like to schedule a 90-min sync to align owners.
3) Patrick, please confirm the canonical tokenizer version and share any fast-fix patches if available. A link to the model manifest would also help.

CCing Soojin (runtime), Evelyn (security) and Alan (product infra) to scope risk and timeline. If we can get the manifest and tokenizer checksum today I'll triage the staging run for tomorrow.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: stratton-lite-v2-manifest.json (metadata only), compat-smoke-plan.md

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Patrick O'Neill <patrick@stratton.ai>, Stratton Labs Model Ops <deploy@stratton.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Alan Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Action] Stratton-lite v2: staged version hold + interop questions

+1 on the 7-day hold until we validate a few things. Operational notes / asks from runtime:

- For the smoke run I need: tokenizer files (vocab/merges/checksums), a small representative prompt set (we can use our internal longform set), and prebuilt quantized artifact if you want us to mirror production memory usage.
- Please indicate whether this model introduces any custom CUDA kernels or fused ops; if yes, we'll need the kernels’ license and build instructions.
- We'll run: tokenization diff, KV memory profile at 1k/2k/4k, and a prefix-cache correctness test. Expect initial results within 24 hours of artifacts.

Patrick — can you drop the manifest and tokenizer checksum to the Drive link Logan included? If you want, we can also run a lightweight canary on a single Dedicated node (no customer traffic) after successful staging.

Subject: Re: [Action] Stratton-lite v2: staged version hold + interop questions

Thanks Logan / Soojin — appreciate the careful approach. Quick clarifications:

- Tokenizer: we're shipping the SentencePiece-based tokenizer. Attached in the Drive folder is tokenizer.spm + checksums.txt. The merge divergence you saw is likely due to a pre-token normalization tweak between our training pipeline and your tokenization. We can produce a patch that reintroduces the old normalizer (low effort).
- No custom CUDA kernels in this build; we use standard ops only. The artifact we shared is float16; a quantized int8 flavor is available but not yet public.
- Manifest: uploaded as stratton-lite-v2-manifest.json (metadata only). Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/stratton-manifest-v2

I'll follow up with a one-pager on the normalization change by EOD. Happy to hop on a quick meeting — how does Wed 11/18 10:00 PT look?

—Patrick
Patrick O'Neill
Head of Model Ops, Stratton Labs
patrick@stratton.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Patrick O'Neill <patrick@stratton.ai>
Cc: Alan Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Action] Stratton-lite v2: staged version hold + interop questions

Thanks for the heads-up. From a security/compliance standpoint we have two quick gate items before we can clear Hosted exposure:

1) Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and model usage terms — we need the DocuSign-ready DPA in place (Stratton legal). I see a DocuSign placeholder in related_links but please confirm execution timeline.
2) Auditable telemetry — during the staging runs we must capture request-level tokenization diffs and suffix-match failure rates and store them in a customer-isolated trace (no raw customer inputs). This is non-negotiable for Dedicated customers on regulated tiers.

If both can be satisfied within the staged hold window we can fast-track to a limited canary; otherwise we'll extend the hold and schedule a formal exception review.

Subject: Re: [Action] Stratton-lite v2: staged version hold + interop questions

Summary and next steps — decision to apply a short staged hold (7 days) starting now. Rationale: tokenizer divergence + KV memory delta + pending DPA. Action items and owners: 

- Stratton: upload tokenizer patch and confirm DocuSign DPA ETA (Patrick) — due: EOD Mon 11/22.
- Runtime: run smoke plan and deliver tokenization diff and KV profile (Soojin) — kickoff Wed 11/18; results Wed 11/18 EOD.
- Security: prepare telemetry hooks and retention plan for the canary (Evelyn) — ready by Thurs 11/19.
- Product Infra: lock model-catalog entry to prevent automated rollout (Alan) — completed now.

If all items land within the hold window we'll move to a single-node canary on Dedicated with strict routing and rollback hooks. If not, we'll request an exception review and extend the hold until mitigations are in place.

Thanks everyone for the quick coordination. I'll book the Wed 11/18 10:00 PT meeting and share an invite.

Logan Wright
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
